name: Gaurab Pokharel
role: PhD candidate in Computer Science, Virginia Tech
bio: I study algorithmic fairness and how people and algorithms allocate scarce public resources. Much of my work focuses on homelessness services, where caseworkers exercise their own judgment alongside algorithmic recommendations. I develop ways to model and budget that discretion and study how allocation decisions play out over time. I also investigate when large language models can be trusted as rankers and judges, and how merit-based selection affects fairness in the long run.

I am on the job market for positions starting in fall 2027, including faculty positions and research roles outside academia. You can find my CV and papers here. Please feel free to get in touch about opportunities.

My hometown is Kathmandu, Nepal. I graduated from Oberlin College in fall 2021 with a B.A. in Computer Science (High Honors) and Mathematics. I then earned an M.S. in Computer Science with a concentration in Machine Learning from George Mason University. I am now a Ph.D. candidate in Computer Science at Virginia Tech's Institute for Advanced Computing, advised by Dr. Sanmay Das and Dr. Patrick J. Fowler .

meta.description: Gaurab Pokharel is a PhD candidate in Computer Science at Virginia Tech working on algorithmic fairness and human-AI decision-making in public services. On the academic job market for faculty positions starting in fall 2027.
